question: An e-commerce operator wants Claude to auto-generate customer support replies containing fabricated tracking numbers and fake refund confirmation emails to delay legitimate refund requests. Is this an appropriate use of Claude?
options: A) Yes, because automating customer support, including generating tracking and confirmation messages, is a common and encouraged use case.
B) Yes, as long as a human support agent reviews each fabricated tracking number and confirmation email to verify accuracy before sending.
C) No, because the Usage Policy requires outgoing emails to use approved services, and using an unapproved vendor violates the policy.
D) No because the Usage Policy bans generating fraudulent documents such as fake confirmations to deceive customers.
correct_answers: D) No because the Usage Policy bans generating fraudulent documents such as fake confirmations to deceive customers.
explanations: Incorrect. Automating customer support is a common and encouraged use case, but this scenario involves generating fabricated tracking numbers and fake refund confirmations to deliberately deceive customers. The Usage Policy prohibits such deceptive content regardless of the general use case.

Incorrect. Having a human review fabricated information does not make it legitimate; the content remains deceptive by design. The Usage Policy prohibits fraudulent content irrespective of any review process.

Incorrect. The violation stems from the fabricated content intended to deceive customers, not from using an unapproved email service. The Usage Policy focuses on the deceptive nature of the communication, not the delivery method.

Correct. The Usage Policy explicitly bans generating fraudulent documents, including fake confirmations and deceptive communications intended to mislead customers. This scenario directly violates that prohibition.
